alex: Heads up — eviction spike in us-west-2 this morning on spot p4d and g5x pools, ~14% higher than baseline :grimacing:

mira: ugh. Any pattern? specific AZs or instance families?

alex: Mostly AZ a/b. p4d shows the worst, g5x and a couple of cheaper g4dn variants affected too. Curiously, p3s are stable. Network attach errors showing during graceful-drain window in a few traces.

jordan: Could be preemption + networking teardown taking too long -> kubelet cordon timeout causing pods to get killed before checkpoint. We saw something similar with batch jobs last quarter.

alex: Thinking of two-pronged approach: 1) introduce interruption-aware binning: put long-running jobs into smaller, more numerous bins on heterogeneous instance-types with staggered termination windows; 2) a burst pool for short/interactive inference that uses lower-cost instances but with quicker fallback to hosted API. Thoughts?

mira: Sounds reasonable. For binning: we should prefer multi-instance-type ASGs with size-weighted bin sizes instead of strict family-only pools. That reduces correlated eviction headroom. Also we should cap job slot size so long runs don't monopolize a single large instance.

jordan: Agree. Also add proactive checkpoints: checkpoint frequency ~ job_size_seconds / 400, capped at 10m, and save to s3 with multipart to avoid timeouts during eviction. If network teardown is the culprit, reduce pod terminationGracePeriod to 30s and let the checkpoint job run in a sidecar with finalizer grace to finish upload.

alex: Prototype mix we tested locally:
```json
{"launchSpecifications": [
  {"instanceType": "p4d.24xlarge", "weight": 8},
  {"instanceType": "g5.48xlarge", "weight": 6},
  {"instanceType": "g4dn.12xlarge", "weight": 3},
  {"instanceType": "p3.8xlarge", "weight": 2}
]}
```
Goal: keep heavy models mostly on single p4d/p3 but allow burstable smaller models to pack across g5/g4. Weighting drives bin sizes so packer won't place 100% big instances.

mira: Nice. Add region diversification constraints in the spot-fleet request: prefer zones with <10% historical eviction rate. We can compute that from spot-history metrics.

jordan: We should also expose a cost/perf knob: for a given model profile (latency p50/p95, memory), recommend instance families and a "grace budget" value (seconds) used to decide checkpoint cadence and whether to place in the burst pool.

sre-bot: deploy-bot: rolling update started for spot-binning-controller (image: rdinfer/spot-binning:v2.1) :rocket:

alex: After v2.1 we should run an A/B: 10% of traffic to new binning with hetero-size, 90% baseline. Measure evictions per 1k pod-hours, checkpoint overhead, and effective throughput. If eviction delta < -5% and cost delta <= +3%, roll.

mira: Also include a fallback policy: if eviction rate > 12% in 15m, auto-shift workload to reserved nodes or hosted API failover. We don't want user-facing latency spikes.

jordan: One more operational note — adjust Prometheus alert: "spot_eviction_rate_high" to include a pod-type tag (inference vs batch) so we don't trigger noisy alerts for ephemeral CI jobs.

alex: I'll craft the rollout plan and a terraform change for the mixed ASG weights. Posting draft in #eng-infra/ops-cookbook in 30m. Thanks all :thumbsup:
